jobs.title: Executive Director, Growth Strategy — Health100
jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary

CVS Health is seeking an experienced leader to serve as Executive Director (ED), Growth Strategy, supporting Health100 Commercialization. As a key member of the Growth Strategy team, the ED will lead high-impact initiatives, provide strategic counsel, and guide high-performing strategy colleagues in solving the most critical challenges facing our healthcare industry.

This role will report into the Head of Growth & Profitability for Health100 and partner frequently with Health100 and CVSH business leaders at EVP and SVP level. The ED will lead strategic, operational, and fiscal initiatives that span the Health100 portfolio, working across business units to identify growth and partnership opportunities. This role can be remote or hybrid with expectation for 10-20% travel for in-person meetings with senior leaders and business teams

Key Responsibilities

Growth Strategy Development & Execution:
Define long-term growth strategy for various healthcare sectors that Health100 is pursing
Identify opportunities to enhance overall go-to-market strategy and capabilities through external partnerships
Support client and external partner conversations and lead working sessions with external stakeholders
Be a key leader on ad-hoc strategy projects for Health100 leadership, including scoping, managing cross-functional teams, and creating executive-ready presentations

Market & Competitive Intelligence:
Monitor emerging industry trends, competitor actions, and disruptive forces across the Health100 portfolio to develop and deliver actionable strategic insights to the Health100 Leadership Team on an ongoing basis

Stakeholder Management:
Effectively facilitate large scale meetings and strategic workshops, including preparation and driving tangible outcomes.
Develop materials with internal and external audiences, including audiences such as ELT leaders and Board of Directors.
Collaborate with other enterprise teams including Corporate Development, Ventures, Finance, Legal, Government Affairs, Technology and Clinical

Talent & Culture Leadership:
Support building and leading a high-performing strategy through execution team and foster a culture of strategic thinking, data-driven decision-making, and innovation.
Directly manage and serve as mentor for junior strategy team members to strengthen the leadership team and the team’s ability to serve as strategic advisors to executives

Required Qualifications

15+ years of related experience at a top management consulting firm, in-house strategy team at a large health care company, investment bank, PE, venture capital or a related growth / strategy focus in a health care setting
Requires significant subject matter expertise across healthcare, primarily Pharmacy and/or pharmacy benefit management, health plans, and life sciences
Experience in digital ecosystems and AI-led automation is preferred
Proven track record of managing a portfolio of projects and initiatives simultaneously, and leading cross-functional teams, including external advisors, on strategy deep dive projects
Ability to lead a high-performing small team that provides consistent error-free analysis and recommendations to ELT and Board level stakeholders

Education

Bachelor’s Degree Required
MBA Degree Preferred

Pay Range

The Typical Pay Range For This Role Is

$131,500.00 - $303,195.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

jobs.title: Associate Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
Lutheran Community Services NW is a non-profit organization dedicated to serving communities throughout Washington, Oregon, and Idaho with a wide range of services for individuals of all ages and backgrounds. All LCSNW team members will contribute to our mission of partnering with individuals, families and communities for health, justice and hope

Compass Housing Alliance is the housing, essential services, and emergency shelter division of Lutheran Community Services Northwest (LCSNW). Compass is guided by the belief that “Everyone Deserves a Home”. We envision a world in which every person lives in a safe, caring community. In this role, you will be employed by Lutheran Community Services Northwest, but work in the Compass division, supporting a 105-year legacy of housing, shelter, and caring in the Puget Sound region.

To learn more about the agency, visit www.compasshousingalliance.org

WHAT WE WILL DO FOR YOU:

As an employer of choice, we’re deeply committed to supporting our employees, because when you’re empowered, our mission thrives. We provide resources, tools, and care that allow you to focus on what matters most: delivering Health, Justice, and Hope
to the communities we serve. We’re proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and peace of mind

A 37.5 per hour work week to ensure work/life balance
Medical, dental, vision, and prescription benefits to keep you and your loved ones healthy
Employer-paid short- and long-term disability insurance
Life insurance coverage at no cost to you
Up to 2 weeks of vacation in your first year (based on hours worked)
Up to 2 weeks of sick leave (based on hours worked)
12 paid agency recognized holidays
2 floating holidays to use your way
403(b) retirement plan with employer matching (eligibility applies)
Access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family
Potential eligibility for Student Loan Forgiveness through our 501(c)(3) nonprofit status

HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

All LCSNW team members will contribute to our mission of partnering with individuals, families and communities for health, justice and hope. The Associate Director of Advancement leads philanthropic activities for the Compass division and other assigned programs or geographic areas in alignment with LCSNW’s organizational strategy and mission. This position provides advancement leadership for Compass, guiding fundraising efforts, donor engagement, and the work of assigned Advancement staff in support of divisional priorities. The Associate Director strengthens alignment between Compass and organizational advancement practices while partnering across the Advancement team to advance shared philanthropic priorities.

Lead advancement activities for assigned division(s), programs, or geographic areas, translating organizational philanthropic strategy into fundraising priorities, plans, and measurable outcomes.
Advise the Director of Philanthropic Strategy and operational leaders on fundraising opportunities, donor trends, community relationships, and emerging needs that may inform philanthropic strategy and priorities.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with individual, corporate, foundation, faith-based, and community donors to expand philanthropic support and develop lasting partnerships.
Oversee assigned advancement portfolios, including annual planning, donor pipelines, revenue forecasting, stewardship activities, performance reporting, and donor data management.
Partner with Advancement team members, operational leaders, Communications, and other stakeholders to coordinate fundraising activities, strengthen donor engagement, and advance consistent organizational practices.
Direct the work of assigned Advancement staff across donor cultivation, stewardship, events, community engagement, and other fundraising activities, ensuring effective execution and progress toward established goals.
Represent LCSNW with donors, faith communities, businesses, community partners, and other stakeholders, building inclusive relationships that strengthen awareness, engagement, and philanthropic investment.
This job is responsible for supervising employees and/or non-employees, such as interns or volunteers. This includes and is not limited to making employment decisions; setting and communicating clear goals in alignment with relevant objectives and required outcomes; and effectively managing individual and team performance

HOW YOU WILL BE A GREAT FIT:

Five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising, development, donor relations, or advancement within a nonprofit or mission-driven organization, including experience leading staff, complex portfolios, or cross-functional initiatives.
Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Communications, Business, or a related field; substantial relevant experience may be considered in place of the degree.
Demonstrated success cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors and managing major gift portfolios, corporate partnerships, community fundraising initiatives, and donor engagement activities.
Demonstrated experience developing and carrying out fundraising plans, monitoring revenue goals and donor pipelines, and using performance data to evaluate progress and adjust activities.
Experience guiding and developing staff while coordinating work across multiple teams, programs, geographic areas, or organizational functions.
Strong understanding of donor-centered fundraising practices, ethical standards, donor confidentiality, and accurate constituent data management.
Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to communicate the organization’s mission authentically and effectively to donors, community partners, faith communities, staff, and other diverse audiences.
Strong relationship-building, solicitation, negotiation, presentation, and stewardship skills, with the judgment and discretion needed to manage sensitive donor and organizational matters.
Strategic and analytical thinking skills, with the ability to translate organizational priorities into actionable fundraising plans while balancing planning, execution, evaluation, and changing needs.
Intermediate mastery of business applications and productivity suites and proficiency using fundraising databases or constituent relationship management systems, such as Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce, or Bloomerang.
Demonstrates resilience, awareness, and self-regulation when navigating challenges, conflict, competing priorities, and barriers.
Thrives in a complex environment and works effectively with cross-functional teams to develop and implement strategies that strengthen donor, partner, and stakeholder experiences.
Demonstrates exceptional commitment to serving and advocating for diverse and marginalized populations.
Interact with others and perform tasks in person and through the use of technology, with long periods of stationary activity and occasional periods of increased physical activity, including sitting, standing, walking, presenting, and participating in events.
Travel regularly between worksites and to donors, community, partner, and event locations, including occasional evening or weekend activities.
Works in a variety of settings, including LCSNW office locations, partner agency and community-based settings, client home or community settings, outdoor settings in varying weather conditions, and faith-based settings such as churches.
Standard LCSNW criminal clearance, including national sex offender. Motor vehicle records, valid driver’s license and auto insurance are required.

Thank you!
We sincerely appreciate your interest in joining the Lutheran Community Services NW team and thank all applicants for taking the time to apply. While we’re unable to respond to every candidate individually, please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Lutheran Community Services NW is deeply committed to our mission of Health, Justice and Hope in all aspects of our work. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences to help us build a stronger, more compassionate community.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
We are excited in your interest to join DC Health (The District of Columbia Department of Health), a nationally accredited public health department (https://phaboard.org/) Where our Vision is for Washington, D.C. to be the healthiest city in America. We believe that all people - no matter their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, education level, age, language, religion, ability, or geographic location - should have the opportunity to live healthy lives.

DC Health is focused on providing the essential public health services (10 Essential Public Health Services) necessary to protect and promote the health of all people in all communities and remove systemic and structural barriers that have resulted in health inequities through the Core Competencies for Public Health Professionals (PH Core Competencies.)

Role

Bring your professional career to Washington, D.C., the most dynamic and diverse city in the country. Join us as you are appreciated, developed, and rewarded and play a vital role in DC Health achieving our Strategic Priorities and Values:

Introduction

This position is located in the Department of Health (DOH), Health Systems and Preparedness Administration (HSPA). DOH promotes health, wellness, and equity across the district, and protects the safety of residents, visitors, and those doing business in the nation’s capital. DOH believes that all people - no matter their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, education level, age, language, religion, ability, or geographic location - should have the opportunity to live healthy lives.

Integral to this role is a strong commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. The Executive Director (Allied Health Boards) actively fosters a culture of diversity, equity, and inclusion within the Department, ensuring that policies and procedures align with these values. They employ anti-racist practices and principles throughout their work, incorporating an anti-racist and anti-oppressive lens into social work practices. Their passion for working in an organization that values and promotes diversity, equity, inclusion, and anti-racism is evident as they contribute to creating such an environment within the Department, making it an essential aspect of their role.

Duties And Responsibilities

Responsible for providing direction for efficient use of Board resources by directing and setting priorities toward achievement of Board goals, track matters pertaining to the Board and assure corrective actions are taken as appropriate. Assists in the process of licensure by examination, endorsement, reinstatement and reactivation of qualified applicants, compiles required documentation and recommends licensure actions to the Board regarding: applicants with a history of disciplinary actions, positive criminal background, etc. Arranges for disciplinary hearings before the Board, obtains and compiles documentation on all reported violations of the District of Columbia law as it related to the various Allied Health Boards, prepares meeting agendas in cooperation with the Board Chairs, and monitors compliance of individuals with any Board sanction.

Represents the Board or Health Systems and Preparedness Administration at meetings and conferences, both within and outside of the District of Columbia. Develops and participates in the orientation of new staff and Board members. Provides leadership and direction to ensure that programs are administered in accordance with applicable Federal and District rules and regulations. Provides testimony for public hearing as the subject matter expert on drafted and current regulations regarding the professions of the Boards. Assigns, directs, and reviews the work of subordinate employees. Evaluates subordinates work performance and recommends and make job selections, promotions, personnel status changes and disciplinary actions together with his/her supervisor.

Qualifications And Education

Specialized Experience
:
Specialized experience is experience that is directly related to the position and has equipped the individual with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position. To be creditable, the incumbent must possess at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression.

Preferred Qualifications: The preferred qualifications include major study in an academic field related to the medical field, health sciences, or allied sciences appropriate to the work of the position, along with a minimum of three years of regulatory experience such as medical board operations, healthcare regulation, enforcement, compliance, or similar oversight functions. An advanced degree in medicine, health sciences, public health, or a closely related field is preferred, and experience working with a professional licensing board, particularly one overseeing medical or allied health professions is highly desirable.

LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS

None.

WORKING CONDITIONS and ENVIRONMENT

Work is performed primarily in an office setting, and at community-based service organizations. Incumbent may be required to travel out of town to attend conferences, seminars, meetings, etc.

Other Significant Facts

Tour of Duty:
Monday – Friday 8:15 a.m. - 4:45 p.m.

Promotion Potential:
None

Duration of Appointment:
MSS At-Will-This position is not in the collective bargaining unit. Management Supervisory Services (MSS): At-Will employment applies to the MSS. All positions and appointments in the MSS serve at the pleasure of the appointing authority and may be terminated at any time with or without cause.

Pay Plan, Series and Grade:
MS-0601-14

Position Designation:
Security Sensitive under the guidelines of the DC Personnel Manual. Incumbents of this position are subject to enhanced suitability screening pursuant to Chapter 4 of DC personnel regulations, and are subject to the following checks and test:

Criminal background check.
Traffic record check (as applicable).
Consumer credit check (as applicable).
Reasonable suspicion drug and alcohol test; and
Post-accident or incident drug and alcohol test.

Residency Requirement:
If the position you are applying for is in the Career, Management Supervisory, or Educational Service at an annual salary of one hundred fifty thousand dollars ($150,000) or more, you must establish residency in the District of Columbia within one hundred eighty (180) days of the effective date of the appointment and continue to maintain residency within the District of Columbia throughout the duration of the appointment.

THE ORGANIZATION

The Northeast Community Clinics, a growing Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) with 18 locations serving many parts of Los Angeles County, is recruiting its next Director of Operations/COO. 

THE ORGANIZATION

For almost 50 years, Northeast Community Clinics (NECC) has been providing comprehensive, culturally competent, high quality primary health and a wide variety of specialty care throughout Los Angeles for diverse, underserved communities, regardless of the patients’ financial status.

The range of services provided by the NECC include: Pediatric, prenatal, family planning, adult general medicine, dental, optometry, endocrinology, and 24-hour emergency coverage through on-call physicians.

With a growing budget of $54M and over 400 employees, NECC serves more than 45,000 patients annually. 

Due to a number of current initiatives, including the integration of two physician practices, launching of a Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), new contracts and grants and other programs addressing emerging social determinants of health, NECC is poised for continued acceleration of growth in resources and programs for the communities they serve.

About The Team

415 Presents: Curran Mission Statement

We create extraordinary live experiences that are commercially successful, culturally meaningful, and uniquely San Francisco. We honor the Curran’s legacy while reimagining how a theater generates lasting value for artists, audiences, our community, and our business.

415 Presents: Curran Core Values

Stewardship: Honor the legacy. Invest in the future.

We preserve the history of the Curran while ensuring it thrives for generations to come.

Curation: Design experiences—not simply events.

Every performance, partnership, and audience touchpoint is intentionally crafted to create something memorable.

Sustainability: Commercial success creates freedom to keep innovating.

We build a financially healthy business that fuels artistic ambition, community investment, and long-term growth.

Impact: Use our stage to strengthen artists, audiences, and community.

We believe live entertainment can revitalize neighborhoods, improve well-being, inspire creativity, and bring people together.

About The Role

415 Presents will assume executive management of the historic Curran Theatre in April 2027. The Managing Director will serve as the senior administrative and strategic leader for the venue, overseeing day-to-day operations, revenue management, administrative functions, and serving as the primary contact for business operations.

The Managing Director will bring the vision for the theater to life: re-establishing the Curran as the most desired stage in San Francisco, where legacy inspires innovation and live entertainment moves our community forward. The Managing Director will work in close coordination with Ambassador Theatre Group (ATG)—who will continue booking Broadway content and supporting key operations. This role will be a dynamic, community minded ambassador who brings strong communication skills, sound financial judgment, creativity and collaborative leadership to operations, programming, and community relations.

Roles & Responsibilities

You’re Excited About This Opportunity Because….

Organizational Leadership & Strategy

Provide overall leadership, vision, and operational direction for the venue in alignment with 415 Presents’ mission, core values, and strategic pillars for Curran Theatre.
Lead the conception and operational execution of a 2027–2029 roadmap, ensuring key milestones, facility enhancements, and partner activations are met.
Champion our team mantra: Every performance should leave the artist, the audience, and our city better than we found them .
Foster a collaborative, high-performing team culture across administrative, facility, and event staff.

Business Operations & Administration

Oversee day-to-day venue operations, administrative workflows, system efficiencies, and staff management.
Serve as the primary liaison between venue ownership (415 Presents / SF Giants), primary operating partners (ATG), title partners, content promoters, and community stakeholders.
Ensure full compliance with all relevant municipal, licensing, and safety regulations.
Oversee capital planning and facility enhancements, including backstage/artist space upgrades and technical systems.
Familiarity of local labor union requirements for venues is a major plus.

Financial Management

Lead the annual budget process, programming P&Ls, long-range financial forecasting, and cash flow monitoring in partnership with ownership.
Drive sustainable commercial growth by maximizing earned revenue through ticket sales, private events, concessions/bar, and commercial venue rentals.
Evaluate financial performance continuously, implementing strategies to enhance operational efficiency and profitability.

Programming Oversight & Curation

Partner with ATG to support their 50-night Broadway content deliverable while actively building the remaining annual show calendar.
Oversee booking expansion into live music, comedy, local productions, and private events.

About The Opportunity

About the Center for Health Policy and Law:

The Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL), “The Center” promotes innovative solutions to public health challenges at home and around the globe. The Center advances law and policy reforms to strengthen population health, reduce health disparities, nourish public health programs, and enhance access to affordable, high-quality healthcare. Housed in the School of Law and firmly rooted in Northeastern University’s nine academic colleges and international network of campuses, the Center brings together Northeastern faculty, students, and experts across disciplines to share knowledge; conduct and disseminate research; and influence the formulation and implementation of health policy and law.

About The Salus Populi

Salus Populi: Educating the Judiciary about the Social Determinants of Health (SP) is a project in collaboration with the Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL) at Northeastern University School of Law and the Institute for Health Equity and Social Justice Research (Institute) at Northeastern University that seeks to provide guidance and training to judges and lawyers on the impact of the law on the social determinants of health (SDOH). Funded by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) and the Kellogg Foundation (Kellogg), CHPL has received grants to train judges about the SDOH, with the goal of moving judges to render decisions that support health equity. The program also trains lawyers and other court personnels. The SP judicial education program is a tuition-free, interactive, and discussion-oriented course that provides judges with the tools they need to recognize how the SDOH impact the issues that come before courts and to read and evaluate public health research relating to the SDOH. The program is offered in Boston and virtually, and other locations with local partners, like San Francisco, Cleveland and North Dakota.

Since its start, SP has trained over 2100 attendees from all over the country. The team consists of faculty and staff from both CHPL and the Institute.

Position Summary

CHPL is seeking a Program Director to oversee projects and deliverables within the Salus Populi (SP) portfolio. This position operates on a hybrid schedule, requiring some in-person days on the Boston campus.

The Program Director will have overall responsibility for the daily functioning of the SP program and work with other members of the SP Leadership team on all aspects of program development and implementation. The Program Director will be responsible for creating and implementing curriculum, organizing events, supervising program staff, and fostering collaboration partnerships. The Program Director will manage the budget and support the development of grant proposals, facilitate meetings, organize events, present at conferences, work with external partners, supervise staff, supervise law students and be adept at project management. The Program Director will serve the mission of SP by helping to train judges, lawyers and other court personnel on the SDOH. We are looking for an attorney who wants to be part of a team that has a passion for health equity, public health policy and law.

Continuation of the appointment beyond 11/1/27 is anticipated but remains contingent upon funding availability

Extensive knowledge of public health law and health policy.

Demonstrated commitment to health equity and belonging and the ability to work with a diverse group of students, staff, and faculty.
Strong attention to detail and proven ability to successfully plan, execute, and monitor complex projects with multiple stakeholders and deliverables.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, this includes the ability to facilitate meetings, conduct presentations and draft reports and legal arguments.

About The Opportunity

About the Center for Health Policy and Law:

The Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL), “The Center” promotes innovative solutions to public health challenges at home and around the globe. The Center advances law and policy reforms to strengthen population health, reduce health disparities, nourish public health programs, and enhance access to affordable, high-quality healthcare. Housed in the School of Law and firmly rooted in Northeastern University’s nine academic colleges and international network of campuses, the Center brings together Northeastern faculty, students, and experts across disciplines to share knowledge; conduct and disseminate research; and influence the formulation and implementation of health policy and law.

About The Salus Populi

Salus Populi: Educating the Judiciary about the Social Determinants of Health (SP) is a project in collaboration with the Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL) at Northeastern University School of Law and the Institute for Health Equity and Social Justice Research (Institute) at Northeastern University that seeks to provide guidance and training to judges and lawyers on the impact of the law on the social determinants of health (SDOH). Funded by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) and the Kellogg Foundation (Kellogg), CHPL has received grants to train judges about the SDOH, with the goal of moving judges to render decisions that support health equity. The program also trains lawyers and other court personnels. The SP judicial education program is a tuition-free, interactive, and discussion-oriented course that provides judges with the tools they need to recognize how the SDOH impact the issues that come before courts and to read and evaluate public health research relating to the SDOH. The program is offered in Boston and virtually, and other locations with local partners, like San Francisco, Cleveland and North Dakota.

Since its start, SP has trained over 2100 attendees from all over the country. The team consists of faculty and staff from both CHPL and the Institute.

Position Summary

CHPL is seeking a Program Director to oversee projects and deliverables within the Salus Populi (SP) portfolio. This position operates on a hybrid schedule, requiring some in-person days on the Boston campus.

The Program Director will have overall responsibility for the daily functioning of the SP program and work with other members of the SP Leadership team on all aspects of program development and implementation. The Program Director will be responsible for creating and implementing curriculum, organizing events, supervising program staff, and fostering collaboration partnerships. The Program Director will manage the budget and support the development of grant proposals, facilitate meetings, organize events, present at conferences, work with external partners, supervise staff, supervise law students and be adept at project management. The Program Director will serve the mission of SP by helping to train judges, lawyers and other court personnel on the SDOH. We are looking for an attorney who wants to be part of a team that has a passion for health equity, public health policy and law.

Continuation of the appointment beyond 11/1/27 is anticipated but remains contingent upon funding availability

JD or equivalent degree and at least 3 years of relevant work experience (e.g. higher education, public health, nonprofit, legal practice, government).
Extensive knowledge of public health law and health policy.

Demonstrated commitment to health equity and belonging and the ability to work with a diverse group of students, staff, and faculty.
Strong attention to detail and proven ability to successfully plan, execute, and monitor complex projects with multiple stakeholders and deliverables.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, this includes the ability to facilitate meetings, conduct presentations and draft reports and legal arguments.
Must be self-directed, able to make independent decisions.

A MPH or equivalent degree

Strategic Leadership and Supervision

Serve as a mentor and supervisor for staff, student interns and research assistants, fostering their growth and development within the organization

Research and draft academic papers and other deliverables;
